questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, must a driver yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just like you would for oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and turn only when it is clear of all traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than not driving defensively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving based on weather, how you feel, and the actions of other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed. Look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights, you have enough room to safely return to your lane.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline mean?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross it to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines show lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: On a one-way street, when can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you increase your speed before turning.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, unless there is a sign saying you cannot. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: Who must a left-turning driver yield to?
questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming cars going straight. You can only turn when it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Must drivers always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Drivers must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road, no matter which direction you are traveling. Always be careful around children.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: What are bicycles considered when used on roadways?
questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: What should you do if your wheels drop off the roadway edge?

options.text: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the roadway.
Turn back onto the roadway immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the roadway.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the roadway immediately. Instead, reduce speed, check for traffic, and gradually turn back when safe.

questions.question: Can drivers park in the handicap parking access aisles next to handicap parking stalls?
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: No one can park in handicap parking access aisles. These aisles must stay clear for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther back from other vehicles. Your car will take longer to stop than it would on dry roads.

questions.question: When driving on the freeway behind a large truck, you should drive:

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Follow farther behind large trucks because they have larger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same road rights as other vehicles. Give motorcycles a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to see you and stay out of your way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to leave room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out of a parked vehicle without looking. A driver may start their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign mean?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work is happening.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn drivers about construction, maintenance, or emergency work ahead.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Always make sure you can safely change lanes before passing. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes and there is clearly enough space for you to move safely.

questions.question: On a two-way, two-lane street, you can only pass safely if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street, you must clearly see the road ahead, be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have a vehicle fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for all lane changes.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal, check all mirrors, and look over your shoulder. Looking over your shoulder checks your blind spot to make sure no vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles are in the next lane.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view. You should:

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move forward slowly into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and you can safely complete the turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided roadway is ending. You are entering a road with traffic going both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicles.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, road work vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. It looks orange during the day and red at night.

questions.question: In rainy weather, you should be most careful when turning or stopping:

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Car oil has not yet washed away from the road. This oil mixes with rain and creates a slippery surface.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children:

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking beside the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, you should:

options.text: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. If you are following one of these vehicles, be ready to stop at railroad tracks.

questions.question: If someone has consumed alcoholic drinks, what will help the person overcome the influence of those drinks?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol on a person.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a crosswalk. Watch for pedestrians crossing the road.

questions.question: You need to use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian using a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is a police officer.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: It is illegal to follow within ____ of an emergency vehicle that is responding to an emergency.
questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet
questions.explanation: Stay back from emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. It is illegal to follow within 500 feet of an emergency vehicle responding to an emergency.

questions.question: A U-turn is not permitted:

options.text: On or near any curve or hill.
On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near any curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and may cause a crash.
